clock t from -1 to 9
noaxes

D2 = segment(2, 2 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 2)))))) thick color 1
D3 = segment(3, 3 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 3)))))) thick color 1
D4 = segment(4, 4 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 4)))))) thick color 1
D5 = segment(5, 5 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 5)))))) thick color 1
D6 = segment(6, 6 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 6)))))) thick color 1
D7 = segment(7, 7 + 1.6*exp(i*(pi/2 - 0.675/(1 + exp(-8*(t - 7)))))) thick color 1

L1 = label(1 - 0.35i, "P(1)")

L5 = label(5 - 0.35i, "P(5)")
L6 = label(6 - 0.35i, "P(6)")
L7 = label(7 - 0.35i, "P(7)")
K0 = arrow(0.15 + 2i, 0.85 + 2i) color 4
K1 = arrow(1.15 + 2i, 1.85 + 2i) color 4
K2 = arrow(2.15 + 2i, 2.85 + 2i) color 4
K3 = arrow(3.15 + 2i, 3.85 + 2i) color 4
K4 = arrow(4.15 + 2i, 4.85 + 2i) color 4
K5 = arrow(5.15 + 2i, 5.85 + 2i) color 4
K6 = arrow(6.15 + 2i, 6.85 + 2i) color 4
A = arrow(-1.2 + 1.4i, -0.1 + 1.4i) thick color 2
> show D0, D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6, D7, L0, L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, L6, L7 | A domino for each statement: $P(0)$, $P(1)$, $P(2)$, and so on. A domino down is a statement proved.
> show K0, K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, K6 | The step, $P(n) \to P(n+1)$ for every $n$: each domino stands where its fall knocks over the next. By itself it knocks nothing over.
> show A; play t to 9 in 6s | The base case: push the first. Then each falls in turn, however far along the line it stands.
